@film is a real frame of the film this shot belongs to. Match its realism exactly: same camera, same lens, same daylight, same colour, same grain. Another frame shot the same day at the same river.

A VERY WIDE LANDSCAPE SHOT OF A BIG RIVER. The camera is FAR OUT over the middle of a wide river, high above the water, looking across at the far bank in the distance. This is a distant landscape view, not a shot of people: the people are incidental specks in it.

COMPOSITION: the river fills the LOWER HALF of the frame — deep, opaque, dark brown-green water in huge volume, running left to right, standing waves and white rapids, spray, no rocks and nothing to stand on, no near bank. Across the MIDDLE of the frame, far away, a thin horizontal band: the far bank's grassy lip and a narrow strip of clearing. Above it a TALL WALL OF RAINFOREST filling the upper third — big trees towering over the bank — and a little pale sky.

THE THREE MEN ARE TINY, DISTANT FIGURES on that far bank, standing still and facing the camera across the water. Each man is only ONE SEVENTEENTH of the frame height: much shorter than the grass clumps beside them, dwarfed by the trees behind them, no larger than a fingertip held at arm's length. Their faces and hands are not resolvable at all — they read only as three small coloured shapes. THEY MUST BE TINY. Do not bring the camera closer to them and do not enlarge them.

Their order and heights: on the LEFT @explorer, the TALLEST, a maroon-red cap and dark doublet over maroon breeches. In the MIDDLE @guide, the SHORTEST, bare-chested with a pale cream wrap. BEHIND and slightly RIGHT of them, set further back, @soldier, height between the two, a tall dark hat and a rust-brown coat. Hands empty.

No haze, no mist, no god rays, no sun shafts. Plain hard tropical daylight like @film. No text, no border, no letterbox bars.

nodes.title: PROMPT · v02 (1203 chars · verbatim from the prompt embedded in the landed MP4)
widgets_values:
ONE UNBROKEN LIVE-ACTION TAKE. NO FADE, NO DISSOLVE, NO CROSS-FADE, NO BLENDING OF TWO PICTURES, NO GHOSTING, NO SOFTENING, NO CUT. Every frame is a sharp, fully detailed photograph of the same place.

The camera is on a crane pulling BACKWARDS over the river, already moving on the first frame and still moving on the last, at one steady speed. It travels in a straight line, back and gently up. The whole change of size comes from that physical travel: real parallax, near grass sliding past faster than the far trees. No zoom.

As the camera retreats: the two men keep walking toward it out of the tall grass and steadily become smaller in frame. A third man in a tall dark hat and rust-brown coat steps out of the grass behind them and follows, staying behind them. The grassy lip of the bank drops into the bottom of frame and dark fast river water appears below it, growing until it fills the lower half of the frame — deep water running left to right, standing waves, white rapids. The three men reach the edge of the bank and stop, standing still and facing the camera across the water.

Same hard tropical daylight, same colour, same grain and same lens for all ten seconds. No text, no border.

widgets_values: The reference images are frames of one actor from a documentary re-enactment: a European explorer of about 1537 with a soft maroon-red cloth cap with a small soft brim, long dark wavy hair to the shoulders, a full dark beard, a grey-mauve quilted doublet belted at the waist, FULL MAROON BREECHES THAT REACH DOWN TO THE KNEE, pale cream mud-stained hose below them, tall brown leather boots with folded-over tops, WHITE SHIRT CUFFS showing at both wrists, and on the front of his belt a BROAD FLAT PALE-STEEL BLADE hung beside a large plain bright metal ring, with a BRIGHT RED POUCH next to it. Make ONE character reference sheet of this man. ONE THING CHANGES FROM THE PREVIOUS SHEET AND EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS. THE MAROON LOWER GARMENT IS A SMOOTH KNEE-LENGTH SKIRT, NOT BREECHES. It hangs straight and flat with a soft A-line and has NO SEPARATION BETWEEN THE LEGS — no inner-leg seam, no split, no gathered or paned or blousy breeches — and its HEM SITS ABOVE THE KNEE. Below the hem, pale cream mud-stained hose, wound and wrapped. This is read off frames 260.600 and 252.500, where no inner-leg line is visible at any magnification. KEEP EXACTLY AS THEY WERE: the soft maroon cap with the downturned brim, the long dark wavy shoulder-length hair, the full dark beard, the grey-mauve quilted doublet with its short flared skirt and white shirt cuffs at both wrists, the broad dark belt with its large plain metal ring, the broad flat pale-steel blade hanging bare over the front, the bright red pouch, and the tall brown boots with folded-over tops. The full-figure profile (259.500) is the identity and proportion anchor. The lower garment is the ONE thing being corrected — build it from 260.600 and 252.500, and do not invent a leg split that the film does not show. Every view must be the SAME man as in the reference images — same face, same age, same skin tone, same hair, same build, same garments, same colours. Do not idealise, do not restyle, do not modernise. Add NOTHING that is not visible in the references: no jewellery, no body paint, no headband, no weapons or props that are not in the frames. Lay it out as a character reference sheet on one neutral mid-grey seamless background under even soft studio light (no jungle, no sunlight, no shadows on the ground). Top row: three head-and-shoulders portraits at the same scale — facing camera, three-quarter, and true profile — eye-line level, neutral expression. Below: a full-body front view and a full-body back view standing straight, feet visible. Along one edge, small detail insets of the hands and of each garment and carried object, close enough to read fabric, stitching and wear. Photoreal, sharp, natural skin texture, no painterly or illustrated look. 3:2 frame. No text anywhere: no labels, no letters, no numbers, no arrows, no captions, no watermark.

# G · R&D STEREO — rebuild Kyle's v03 stereo recipe in Comfy, then test it

**Purpose.** cgi-042 is a stereo CONVERSION shot: generated content, so no camera or interocular data exists for it. Conversions are matched to the film's existing stereo pairs. Kyle's v03 recipe (made OUTSIDE Comfy: fal depth → median5 + atadenoise → Resolve/Fusion mesh comp → eyes → `spatial make`) is the starting point to match. Whether that recipe holds to filmout standard is the open R&D question — it is NOT assumed to be the standard.
This group re-runs the same *stages* inside Comfy on a short window so we can measure it. It branches from the HANDOFF `GetVideoComponents` — nothing left of the HANDOFF frame is rewired.

**Status: BUILT - NOT RUN. (V3b — see CHANGE REPORT note to the right.)** New chain is MUTED (grey) so Queue cannot fail on the unwired depth input. fal node is BYPASSED (purple) so it cannot spend.

## Flow (left to right)
1. `TRIM` — 25-frame window, frames 109-133 (centre = evidence frame 121). Full take = 241 frames; a 4K float batch is ~24 GB RAM per copy.
2. `DEPTH` — fal depth-anything v2, same endpoint v03 used (`fal-ai/image-preprocessors/depth-anything/v2`). 25 calls ≈ $0.025.
3. `STEREO` — Y7 SBS (Video). Outputs ONE side-by-side batch 7680x2160.
4. `SPLIT` — two ImageCrop → eye L / eye R, 3840x2160.
5. `OUTPUT` — three preview SaveVideos (SBS, L, R).

## BISECT RUN — raw frames + depth only (Y7 and the OUTPUT nodes stay muted)
Question being tested: do the decoded frames or the fal depth maps move/pump between frames?
Spend: fal depth on 25 frames ≈ $0.025 — approved by Brynley 2026-10-08.
1. Drag `TRIM · image` → fal depth node `image` input. Drag fal `image` output → `EVIDENCE 2 · SaveImage`.

Later, for the full stereo arm: also drag fal output → `STEREO · depth_maps`, then unmute STEREO + OUTPUT nodes.

- **Not a replica of Kyle's comp.** His comp is a 3D mesh displace (Displace3D 0.346, Camera3D sep 0.064, conv/z 4.82, AoV 19.264) in Resolve/Fusion. - **Filmout path is UNVERIFIED, not ruled out.** These outputs use core `SaveVideo` with codec/format left on `auto`; what it writes (codec, bit depth) has not been checked. ProRes (e.g. VideoHelperSuite Video Combine) and image-sequence/EXR writers exist, but their bit-depth path through Comfy has not been tested. Until a test frame is written and probed (ffprobe/exiftool), treat these outputs as comparison material, not delivery.
- **Node packs:** needs `ComfyUI-Y7-SBS-2Dto3D` and `ComfyUI-fal-API` (README pins). Missing packs show red.
- **fal node name is by convention** (`FalAPI_` + endpoint with slashes → dashes) and its socket names were NOT verified. If red, add the depth node by search instead.
